name: Bengaluru Tenant Security Deposit Withholding
raw_input: I was renting a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru for 2 years at Rs 28,000/month. I gave 1 lakh rupees as security deposit. I gave proper 1-month notice on 1st October and vacated the flat on 31st October 2024. I cleared all electricity and water bills and handed over keys. Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days. Now it has been 25 days, he stopped picking my calls, and yesterday he messaged saying he is deducting Rs 45,000 for 'complete house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning'. There was no damage, just normal nail holes for photo frames and standard wear and tear. I have move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat where he acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition. How can I get my Rs 45,000 back?

case_dossier.case_title: Arbitrary Security Deposit Deduction for Normal Wear and Tear
case_dossier.summary: The landlord, Mr. Ramesh, withheld Rs. 45,000 from the tenant's security deposit of Rs. 1,00,000 for house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning after the tenant vacated the premises in good condition. The tenant has cleared all utility bills, given proper notice, and possesses comprehensive proof including move-in/move-out records and WhatsApp acknowledgments.

timeline.event: Tenant gave proper 1-month notice to vacate the 2BHK flat.
Tenant vacated the flat, cleared all electricity and water bills, and handed over keys.
Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the security deposit via UPI.
Landlord stopped picking calls and sent a message deducting Rs. 45,000 for repainting, polishing, and deep cleaning.

evidence_held: WhatsApp chat where the landlord acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition
evidence_needed: Copy of the signed Rent Agreement (to verify clauses regarding painting, cleaning, and security deposit refund timelines)
Written formal demand/legal notice or final written response sent to the landlord
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: The evidence strength is high due to comprehensive documentation including handover videos, move-in/move-out records, and direct WhatsApp acknowledgments from the landlord.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
You are well-protected under Indian tenancy law regarding the return of your security deposit, as routine wear and tear cannot be charged to you. Under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, tenants are only responsible for returning the property in its original condition subject to normal wear and tear. Your comprehensive evidence, including WhatsApp chats and handover videos, places you in a very strong legal position to recover your withheld funds.

Key Legal Rule: Normal aging, minor scuffs, and routine wear and tear are legally the landlord's responsibility, and unauthorized deductions from your security deposit constitute a civil breach of contract.

Immediate Takeaway: Do not file a criminal complaint, as this is purely a civil dispute; instead, gather your written agreement and serve a formal demand notice for your full refund.

governing_laws.relevance: Protects you from being penalized for reasonable wear and tear, ensuring you are not liable for routine repainting or natural property aging.
Clarifies that withholding a deposit is a civil dispute and breach of contract, preventing improper criminal police complaints.

action_options.title: Serve a Formal Legal Demand Notice
action_options.details: Draft and send a formal written legal notice to the landlord citing Section 108(B)(m) of the Transfer of Property Act, demanding the immediate return of the unlawfully deducted deposit amount using your move-out photos and WhatsApp acknowledgments as proof.

action_options.title: Utilize Free Legal Guidance and Support
action_options.details: If the landlord fails to respond, contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) via helpline 15100 for free legal aid and guidance. Note: DLSA provides free legal aid and guidance only; it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings against a landlord.

action_options.title: File a Recovery Suit before the Civil Court
action_options.details: If the pre-litigation notice and DLSA guidance do not resolve the matter, file a recovery suit for the withheld amount before the local civil court or Small Causes Court using your rent agreement, bank statements, and handover videos.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can initiate a pre-litigation legal notice and approach DLSA for free guidance on your own. However, if you choose to file a formal civil recovery suit in court, consulting a licensed advocate will help ensure your documentation and pleadings are properly structured.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**FROM:**
[Your Name] 
[Your Address] 
Phone: [Your Phone Number] 
Email: [Your Email Address] 

**DATE:** 09/11/2026

**MODE OF DISPATCH:** Speed Post (AD) / Registered Email

**TO:** 
Mr. Ramesh 
[Landlord's Address] 

---

### **SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR THE UNLAWFUL WITHHOLDING AND ARBITRARY DEDUCTION OF SECURITY DEPOSIT**

Sir,

I, am a tenant and former occupant of the residential premises situated at [Property Address]. I hereby serve upon you this formal legal demand notice regarding the arbitrary and unlawful deduction of Rs. 45,000 from my security deposit of Rs. 1,00,000, and I hereby state and submit as under:

1. That on 1st October 2024, I provided you with a proper 1-month notice to vacate the 2BHK flat that I had rented from you.
2. That on 31st October 2024, I completely vacated the flat, cleared all outstanding electricity and water utility bills, and formally handed over the keys back to you.
3. That within 3 days of 31st October 2024, you acknowledged the handover of the premises and explicitly promised to refund my security deposit of Rs. 1,00,000 via UPI.
4. That despite my peaceful surrender of the premises in good condition—which is fully supported by my move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chats where you acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition—you failed to refund the full security deposit.
5. That 25 days post-vacation / yesterday, after you suddenly stopped picking up my phone calls, you sent me a message arbitrarily deducting Rs. 45,000 from my security deposit under the pretexts of house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.
6. That under Section 108(B)(m) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only required to restore the property in as good a condition as it was in at the time he was put in possession, subject to changes caused by reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Normal aging, minor scuffs, and routine property maintenance such as repainting and deep cleaning after a tenancy are legally the landlord's responsibility and cannot be arbitrarily charged or deducted from my security deposit.
7. That your sudden deduction of Rs. 45,000 constitutes an unauthorized withholding of my funds and a civil breach of our tenancy terms, especially in light of your explicit WhatsApp acknowledgments confirming that the flat was returned in good condition.

### **DEMAND**

I, therefore, call upon you through this notice to pay/refund the unlawfully withheld amount of **Rs. 45,000** to my bank account [or via UPI] within **15 days** from the date of receipt of this notice. 

Please note that if you fail to comply with this demand within the stipulated 15-day rectification window, I shall be constrained to initiate appropriate legal proceedings against you before the appropriate civil forum for the recovery of the said amount, along with associated costs. You may also seek free legal guidance from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) via helpline 15100 if required.

Copies of this notice and all supporting evidence are being retained for future legal action.

Sincerely / Yours faithfully,

*(Signature)* 
[Your Name]

---

### **ANNEXURE INVENTORY**
1. Move-in photos
2. Move-out handover video
3. All rent payment bank statements
4. WhatsApp chat screenshots showing landlord's acknowledgment of the flat in good condition
5. Copy of the signed Rent Agreement [if applicable]

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Mr. Ramesh, as per Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, ordinary wear and tear like wall paint aging cannot be deducted from my deposit. I have the handover video and our chat proof. Please refund my balance 45,000 within 7 days.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre sahab, sections mat sunao mujhe! Agreement clause 14 padha hai kya? Har tenant ko flat waise hi dena padta hai jaise mila tha. Cleaning aur painting ka kharcha toh aana hi hai, sab log yahi karte hain. Chalo theek hai, zyada jhanjhat mat karo, main 20,000 kaat kar baaki bhej deta hoon, final settlement maan lo.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You firmly cited the Transfer of Property Act and Model Tenancy principles regarding normal wear and tear, and backed it up with concrete evidence like handover videos and WhatsApp chats.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Do not accept his partial offer of 20,000. Reiterate that no deductions are permissible for normal wear and tear under law, and demand the full Rs. 45,000.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Mr. Ramesh, normal wear and tear is legally excluded from deductions, and my video proof shows the property was returned in good condition; I expect the full Rs. 45,000 without any arbitrary cuts.
